answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind an agent’s history to a succinct proof, while verifiable delay primitives enforce a unique time-ordered nonce, ensuring that any attempt to clone an identity must rerun the computation over a growing thread of state, incurring exponential work; this information-theoretic barrier renders spoofing as hollow as a comet’s fleeting tail, making forgery infeasible under standard cryptographic hardness assumptions.
